87 RMG factories shut amid Tk30,000 wage demand
item.description:
At least 87 readymade garment (RMG) factories in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur remained closed on Wednesday as workers renewed protests demanding a monthly minimum wage of Tk30,000, hours after the Minimum Wage Board fixed the new minimum wage at Tk17,000.
Clashes between workers and police erupted across the three industrial areas, disrupting production and traffic as authorities moved to contain the unrest.
According to industrial police and local sources, 55 factories in Gazipur and 32 in Savar and Ashulia remained closed amid demonstrations and work stoppages.
In Savar's Hemayetpur area, workers joined their morning shifts before walking out and attempting to block the Hemayetpur-Singair road and the Padma Mor area.
Police fired tear gas and sound grenades to disperse the protesters. A police member was reportedly injured after being hit by a brick, while some protesters also threw bricks and stones at a nearby AKH Group factory, local police said.
Ashulia Industrial Police-1 Superintendent Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan said at least 22 factories in the area had declared a holiday for the day.
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel were deployed alongside police, while water cannons and armoured personnel carriers were kept on standby to maintain order across the Savar-Ashulia industrial zone.
The zone houses 736 garment factories, including 470 export-oriented units.
In Gazipur, workers also refused to enter factories and took to the streets, blocking sections of the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in the Sataish area from around 9am, disrupting traffic.
Witnesses said 400-500 workers carrying sticks blocked a branch road in Sataish, triggering chases and counter-chases with police. Officers fired sound grenades to disperse the crowd.
Around 1,000-1,200 workers also blocked Joydebpur road under Gazipur Sadar Metropolitan Police Station at around 9:50am, while several factories declared a general holiday following work stoppages.

item.title: July fighters file writ seeking permanent ban on Awami League
item.description:
Seven July uprising fighters have filed a writ petition with the High Court seeking permanent prohibition and dissolution of the Awami League and all its affiliated, associate and allied organisations, with their designation as “criminal organisations”.
Supreme Court lawyer ASM Shahriar Kabir filed the petition on Wednesday on behalf of the fighters, who were injured by gunfire during the July-August 2024 uprising and continue to carry bullets in their bodies.
The petition, filed under Article 102(2) of the constitution, names nine respondents, including the secretaries of the home, foreign and law ministries, the cabinet secretary, Bangladesh Bank governor and chiefs of the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) and Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC).
The petitioners said they had served legal notices on the respondents on November 19, giving them 24 hours to act, but received no response.
They sought directions for the government to permanently ban and dissolve the party through legislation or an ordinance under Article 93 of the constitution.
The petition also seeks action against individuals and television channels allegedly defending the Awami League, denying or justifying the 2024 killings, or branding July fighters as militants.
It asks relevant authorities to report to the court within 30 days on measures taken under the Penal Code and Anti-Terrorism Act.
Other prayers include removing or blocking the party's online posts, pages, accounts and channels, and initiating legal action against those allegedly financing or supporting armed activities.
The petition argues that the May 12, 2025 government notification banning all Awami League activities pending the completion of trials at the International Crimes Tribunal was temporary, making a permanent legal prohibition necessary.
It also alleges that, despite the ban, party activists have been involved in arson, bomb attacks and killings since November 10, citing several recent incidents across the country.
The petition further seeks an independent judicial inquiry, led by a serving or retired Supreme Court judge, into alleged abuses and violence between 1972 and 2026, with a report to be submitted within 90 days.
It also asks the court to direct the government to pursue diplomatic efforts to have the party listed as a Foreign Terrorist Organization by the United States and seek cooperation from India to prevent its territory from being used for activities against Bangladesh.

item.title: TIB: Large developers have established ‘mafia system’ in real estate sector
item.description:
Despite its contributions to housing, infrastructure and employment, the private real estate sector has come under scrutiny for alleged political influence, administrative collusion and entrenched networks of vested interests that undermine regulatory oversight.
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) said a section of large developers had established a powerful “mafia system” involving political patronage, middlemen, land-based interest groups and informal administrative networks, effectively holding policymaking and the regulatory framework hostage.
The organization made the observations in a research report titled “Challenges of Good Governance in Land Development in the Private Housing Sector in Dhaka City,” released at a press conference. It recommended forming an Inter-Agency Coordination Platform involving Rajuk, the Department of Environment and other relevant organizations and stakeholders, establishing an integrated institutional framework to monitor the housing market, and setting up an Independent Complaint Resolution Board to address customer complaints.
The press conference was attended by TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman, Adviser-Executive Management Professor Sumaiya Khair, Director of the Research and Policy Department Muhammad Badiuzzaman and Senior Research Fellow Shahzada M Akram.
Director of the Outreach and Communication Department Mohammad Touhidul Islam moderated the event, while former Research Fellow of the Research and Policy Department Atanu Das presented the report.
Iftekharuzzaman said: “Real estate companies have made positive contributions in various areas, including housing arrangements and creating housing opportunities, infrastructure development and employment generation. At the same time, they are also making significant contributions to GDP. However, there is no scope to deny the various forms of harassment, corruption, irregularities and land grabbing in this sector.”
The research found allegations of irregular financial transactions to obtain necessary approvals and clearances from government and regulatory institutions. In real estate companies' terminology, these payments are called “speed money” and included in project budgets as “miscellaneous expenses”.
Under normal circumstances, irregular expenditure throughout the process, from company registration to the implementation of a private housing project, ranges from Tk16.50 lakh to Tk37.50 lakh per acre. For a 25-acre private housing project, the estimated expenditure amounts to Tk4.12 crore to Tk9.35 crore.
The report also found allegations that government institutions deliberately delay files even when applications are submitted with all required documents in compliance with regulations, forcing applicants into informal communication and irregular financial transactions.
On the other hand, allegations against developers include delaying plot handovers, unilaterally canceling allocations without informing buyers, delaying refunds and misappropriating payments.
Buyers may have to pay up to approximately Tk14.50 lakh per katha beyond the total plot price in development fees, service charges and utility charges before handover. The amount increases considerably in modern and luxury housing projects.
The research also found that some developers use political influence to expand housing projects by acquiring agricultural land, khas land and land adjacent to rivers at nominal prices or through forceful occupation, without obtaining necessary approvals and clearances.
The involvement of influential politicians, party leaders and their close relatives as shareholders, officeholders or advisers on company boards creates opportunities for political influence and legal protection for irregular activities, the report said.
The research identified policy capture in the real estate sector to protect undisclosed money.
According to the findings, the Real Estate and Housing Association of Bangladesh (REHAB) builds public opinion and policy support through specific narratives and campaigns to influence policy decisions in its favor.
These campaigns present the facility to legalize undisclosed money as the only way to encourage investment, keep the housing market vibrant, increase the flow of money in the economy, generate employment and revenue, and prevent money laundering.
A review of the legal framework found that Section 5(7) of the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010, does not require authorities to consider a company's previous fraudulent activities, irregularities or criminal activities, including breaches of contract, when renewing its registration.
As a result, companies involved in irregularities can easily maintain valid registrations, the report said.
The findings also showed that developers regularly violate policies and laws by exploiting loopholes in existing regulations, weak enforcement and a lack of coordination among authorities. Some companies implement residential projects and sell plots without the necessary approvals and clearances or obtain them retrospectively through irregular means.
An assessment of developers' capacity found that most companies lack the required number of employees, prescribed amounts of land and necessary infrastructure.
REHAB and the Bangladesh Land Developers Association (BLDA) have failed to control the monopolistic and arbitrary activities of large and influential developers. They also lack effective measures to curb unauthorized residential projects and regulate the activities of real estate companies.
The research further identified manpower shortages at Rajuk, the Deputy Commissioner's Office, the Department of Environment, WASA and the Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority as major obstacles to effective supervision.
The report found allegations of irregularities in land selection and acquisition, including the use of khas, government and Nawab Estate lands as part of housing projects.
Some companies allegedly fail to pay landowners the agreed prices or pay only part of the amount while taking possession of the original deeds.
The research also documented allegations of media interference by influential real estate companies. These include obstructing the publication of reports against their interests, pressuring media outlets to remove published reports, intimidating journalists and physically harassing them.
In some cases, journalists and media representatives are allegedly offered unethical financial benefits, plot allocations and other inducements to prevent the publication of investigative reports.
The report said real estate companies regularly provide funding and logistical support to political parties, creating networks of mutual interests that help secure policy protection and unethical business advantages.
Despite changes in ownership following political changes, the practice of using political influence to bypass regulatory rules and procedures has continued, it added.
The influence of housing businessmen in revisions to the Detailed Area Plan (DAP) is reflected in the number of amendments made to the plan. The DAP was amended 158 times between 2010 and 2018.
Within just 1 year of the formulation of the DAP (2022-2035) in 2022, official initiatives were taken at least 4 times to amend it in response to demands from businessmen, while major amendment gazettes were published twice.
Building heights and Floor Area Ratio (FAR) were increased without technical recommendations, while protected wetlands and flood-flow zones were converted into areas suitable for housing, the research found.
Iftekharuzzaman said: “It is essential for the government to take initiatives to control misgovernance and corruption in the housing sector. In this regard, the government will provide the leadership and act as the main catalyst. The government must prepare a roadmap on this issue and involve stakeholders in the process. At the same time, the relevant institutions must be strengthened. A roadmap alone is not enough; the institutions must be given an environment in which they can work independently, along with responsibilities and authority. Similarly, those involved in these crimes must be brought under accountability and effective examples must be set.”
TIB made 13 recommendations to address the problems in the sector, including amendments to the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010, and making annual audits and disclosure of financial information mandatory for real estate companies.
The recommendations also include amending the Private Residential Project Land Development Rules, 2004, which were amended in 2012 and 2015, and developing a comprehensive database for Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and guidelines for Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA).
TIB recommended requiring developers to clearly mention development fees, utility charges and refund policies alongside plot prices in advertisements.
It also called for formulating a specific code of ethical conduct for the sector in line with global best practices and ensuring its effective implementation.
The organization recommended legal action against developers and media outlets involved in advertising plots without valid approvals and clearances.
It further proposed making it mandatory for land acquisition, plot sales and all related financial transactions to take place through banking channels and undergo regular audits.
In cases of illegal occupation of land or waterbodies, projects and land development, TIB recommended legal action against the companies involved, as well as the relevant officials and employees of government regulatory institutions, politically influential individuals and other middlemen involved in the process.

item.title: Home minister: Awami League will never return to politics in Bangladesh
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said the Awami League has lost its status as a political party and transformed itself into a terrorist organisation through its activities, adding that it will never be allowed to return to democratic politics in Bangladesh.
He said the party had lost all legitimacy following its collapse and the departure of its leaders after the genocide committed during the 2024 mass uprising. The people of Bangladesh would never again recognise it as a legitimate political party, he added.
The minister cited the examples of fascist and mafia-like forces, including Nazi Germany, saying organisations responsible for genocide had never been able to return to politics elsewhere in the world. Similarly, the Awami League, whose activities have been banned, would never be able to return to Bangladesh or take part in democratic politics.
He made the remarks at a press briefing on current affairs in the conference room of the Ministry of Home Affairs at the Secretariat on Wednesday.
Asked about the former prime minister's stated intention to return to Bangladesh, Salahuddin said the public, both at home and abroad, was aware of how the fugitive and convicted individual was seeking to return.
He said any such return would have to take place under the framework of an extradition treaty. The government had already communicated with the relevant country through diplomatic channels, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and that country had indicated it would examine the matter in accordance with its laws and take appropriate action.
“How long will this ‘I am coming, I am coming’ narrative continue?” he asked, referring to dates being mentioned, including November, December and specifically December 16.
He said the government was neither concerned nor under pressure over such claims, adding that law enforcement agencies remained on high alert.
The minister alleged that fugitive leaders based in countries to Bangladesh's west and east were directing their remaining followers inside the country to carry out subversive activities, including torchlight processions, lockdowns, shutdowns and general strikes.
He said the leaders were putting their followers at risk by misleading them and warned that the people of Bangladesh would not tolerate such activities.
Salahuddin said law enforcement agencies had so far thwarted attempts by the groups with patience and strategic planning, without any loss of life or damage to property.
He warned that anyone involved in extremist activities, arson or attempts to harm public lives and property would face strict legal action.
On the deployment of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel in different districts, the minister said deploying the force alongside police and other security agencies in areas where intelligence suggests a risk of unrest was a routine security measure.
He added that all necessary security arrangements had been completed under the guidance of the Ministry of Home Affairs to ensure peaceful celebrations of Victory Day.
Asked about a possible ban on the Awami League as a political party, Salahuddin said the matter was part of an ongoing judicial process.
He said the International Crimes (Tribunals) (Amendment) Act, 2026, and Article 47 of the Constitution contained provisions for prosecuting not only individuals but also political parties and organisations for crimes against humanity.
The activities of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations had already been prohibited through an official notification during the interim government's tenure, while the Election Commission had suspended the party's registration, he added.
Asked about sabotage in Gopalganj and the alleged involvement of police officers, the minister said several officers had been arrested based on specific evidence of political bias or involvement in conspiracies while serving in government positions.
They were facing sedition charges as well as departmental proceedings, he said.
He also said an additional superintendent of police who was posted in Muksudpur upazila of Gopalganj and was a resident of the area had recently been withdrawn from duty and placed under closure.
On labour unrest in the garment sector, Salahuddin said the minimum wage had been determined through a democratic process involving representatives of workers and employers under the Wage Board.
He said genuine workers and employers were satisfied with the decision, while those attempting to create disorder in industrial areas by spreading rumours were not actual workers.
The minister alleged that certain groups were exploiting the situation as part of a political conspiracy. He said law enforcement agencies were handling the situation patiently and working to identify those instigating the unrest from behind the scenes.
Asked about discussions with anti-fascist political parties, Salahuddin said the prime minister had already held meetings with several leaders of the National Citizen Party (NCP).
He said the government planned to hold discussions with other political parties as well, with a view to forming an alliance.

item.title: PM directs third-party price assessment for checking costly procurement
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed the authorities concerned to engage independent price assessment companies to scrutinise the procurement costs of major development projects, strengthen manpower planning and promote sustainable construction materials.
State Minister for Planning Md Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki disclosed the directives while briefing journalists today at the NEC conference room after the eighth meeting of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) in this fiscal year (FY27) chaired by the Prime Minister at the Bangladesh Secretariat today.
Saki said the prime minister approved a proposal to involve domestic or foreign price assessment companies in examining the costs of expensive equipment and specialised procurement items.
“Where the expenditure involves a substantial amount, we should appoint price assessment companies to verify the costs. This will introduce independent third-party scrutiny and establish an institutional system of checks and balances,” he said.
The state minister said the Planning Commission had already introduced measures to involve relevant specialists in examining equipment and procurement costs that do not fall under the approved rate schedule.
He said the government was also developing software that would use artificial intelligence (AI) to check whether project expenditure follows the approved rate schedule.
“Individual officials or project authorities may not always have the technical expertise to assess highly specialised equipment. We need an independent verification process so that project costs remain justified and excessive expenditure does not take place,” Saki said.
He said the prime minister specifically directed the authorities to apply the price assessment mechanism during the tender document preparation and procurement processes for the projects involving the construction of medical college hospitals and the expansion of the National Institute of Gastroenterology Hospital.
The prime minister also instructed the authorities to determine the required number of doctors, nurses, technicians and other skilled personnel at the initial stage of healthcare projects.
Saki said the government would no longer wait until projects approach completion to seek manpower approval, a practice that often delays the operation of newly constructed hospitals and leaves expensive equipment unused.
“Manpower approval must come alongside project implementation. The authorities must secure the necessary approval from the Ministry of Public Administration and the Ministry of Finance at the beginning and complete the required training before the project ends,” he said, quoting the prime minister’s direction.
He said the government would also incorporate training requirements into procurement conditions so that equipment suppliers could provide specialised training to medical personnel.
The state minister added that the government planned to increase investment in health education to develop doctors and technicians with the necessary specialised skills.
Saki said the meeting also discussed delays in implementing projects under government-non-government organisation (GO-NGO) partnerships.
He cited a healthcare centre project in Char Fasson upazila of Bhola district, which faced repeated delays because the partner NGO could not provide its committed 20% share of the project cost, while the government was supposed to provide the remaining 80%.
The project received approval for its fourth revision, including a six-month extension.
He said the Planning Ministry had prepared proposals to revise the existing GO-NGO collaboration framework.
“We need to examine how government-NGO partnerships should operate and establish clearer guidelines. The Planning Ministry will discuss the proposals with the relevant ministries before placing the issue at the next National Economic Council meeting,” he said.
The prime minister also directed the authorities to gradually increase the use of uniblock materials in rural road construction under the Herringbone Bond (HB) road development programme.
Saki said the government planned to reduce dependence on traditional brick roads because uniblock roads offer greater durability and can help reduce environmental damage caused by brick kilns.
Under the proposed approach, authorities will use 50% uniblocks and 50% bricks in the first year, 60% uniblocks and 40% bricks in the second year, and 70% uniblocks and 30 % bricks in the third year if the programme continues.
“Although uniblock roads may initially cost more, they offer greater durability and provide better convenience for people. We also want to reduce the environmental damage associated with the expansion of brick kilns,” he said.
The HB Road programme mainly covers rural roads that have not yet received official identification and therefore do not fall under the regular road maintenance responsibilities of the relevant agencies.
Saki said the government wanted to accelerate rural infrastructure development by revising ongoing projects and incorporating additional components rather than spending time preparing entirely new projects.

item.title: Study: Migrant workers recoup only 12-15% of cost after recruitment scams
item.description:
Migrant workers who face recruitment fraud and exploitation abroad recover only 12-15% of their migration costs through mediation, leaving many struggling with debt and financial losses, a new study by the Ovibashi Karmi Unnayan Program (OKUP) has found.
The report, titled “Justice by Procedure? Why Migrant Workers Need Binding Justice, Not Mediation”, reviewed 85 complaints filed under the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training’s (BMET) arbitration system between November 2024 and June 2026.
The complainants included 50 men and 35 women, around 86% of whom had migrated to Saudi Arabia through legal channels.
Male workers spent an average of Tk4.58 lakh to migrate, while female workers spent Tk31,900. Yet compensation recovered through mediation covered only around 15% and 12% of their respective costs.
Of the 85 complaints, 52 remained unresolved, 28 were settled and five had stalled during the study period. Although hearings are supposed to be held within 30 working days, 44% of complaints took up to 12 weeks to initiate proceedings, while 29% of complainants were never called for a hearing.
The study found no evidence of separately documented investigations in any of the 85 cases. Instead, the system relies largely on hearings and negotiated settlements, making it difficult to establish accountability when recruiting agencies deny responsibility or informal brokers are involved.
OKUP Chairperson Shakirul Islam questioned whether the existing system could ensure fair justice, adequate compensation and accountability for recruitment fraud and exploitation.
He said recruiting agencies often wield greater bargaining power, while workers seeking compensation are financially vulnerable and frequently come from remote areas. Agencies can also skip hearings without facing fines or penalties, while workers are pressured to accept settlements that fail to cover their actual losses.
Half of the 28 settled cases resulted in compensation of Tk30,000-Tk50,000. Most female workers who received compensation got between Tk15,000 and Tk30,000.
The study found that 91% of complainants did not receive legally required employment contracts before departure, while 72% had no written contract even after reaching their destination.
Overall, 78% reported job-related fraud, 68% wage-related deception and 42% exploitation. Among female domestic workers surveyed, all reported wage exploitation, 97% psychological abuse, 77% physical abuse and 89% confinement or isolation.
Around 40% of complainants were forced to return to Bangladesh within six months of migration, before completing their initial contracts, leaving many facing severe financial losses and debt.
Although the Overseas Employment and Migrants Act 2013 provides for criminal penalties for recruitment fraud, OKUP said the administrative complaint process increasingly relies on mediation rather than binding remedies.
The report recommends stronger investigations, impartial complaint handling, a structured compensation policy and effective enforcement of remedies.
The findings were presented at an event in Dhaka on Wednesday, attended by officials from the government, the International Labour Organization, the International Organization for Migration and other development organisations.

item.title: Outsider attacks prompt over 50 factories in Gazipur to shut down
item.description:
More than 50 garment factories in the Gazipur industrial zone have announced closures for Wednesday amid ongoing labour unrest and attacks on factories, while workers have begun returning to their village homes.
Authorities at 16 factories have declared a two-day closure on Wednesday and Thursday, while several others have announced shutdowns for security reasons following reports of vandalism.
The information was confirmed through conversations with workers and human resources officials at the affected factories.
With Friday already a weekly holiday, workers at factories closed for two days will have a three-day break. Many have already started leaving for their village homes.
The situation was observed during a visit to the Gazipur industrial zone between Wednesday morning and midday. Law enforcement personnel have been deployed across the industrial area to prevent further incidents.
The 16 factories that have announced a two-day closure are Vintex Denim Ltd, T-Design Knitwear Ltd, D-Zitex Knitwear Ltd, Meghna Knit Composite, Sublime Garments (Meghna Group), Executive Green Tex, Executive High Fashion, Standard Garments, Sustainable Wet Processing, MNR Sweater, MNR Fashion, Welldone Sweater, TS Casual, Euro Fashion, Pandora Sweater and Unisense Garments.
All are located in the Baherarchala area of Sreepur Municipality.
Meanwhile, Color & Fashion Industries Ltd, Denimac Denim, KSS Knitwear Ltd, Taqwa Fashion Ltd and Lantabur Garments, located in Tepirbari village of Telihati Union, have announced one-day closures.
Esrotex Garments, Pastel Apparels, Epic Garments, NASA Hi-Tech and Style Fashion Ltd have announced indefinite closures.
Allegations have emerged that several garment factories were attacked and vandalised on Monday and Tuesday.
The affected establishments include Ratul Apparels Ltd in the South Bhangnahati area, MHC Apparels Ltd in Kewa Notun Bazar, Denimec in Gargariya Masterbari, Hams Garments in South Bhangnahati, Laxma Inwear Ltd, Victoria Garments, Noman Home Textiles Ltd of the Noman Group, and a garment factory in Baghermondol.
In some incidents, groups of people allegedly pushed against factory gates. Where they managed to enter, they vandalised offices and damaged furniture and other property.
Police said the attacks were carried out by outsiders posing as workers in an attempt to create panic among factory owners, officials and employees.
Amjad Hossain, superintendent of police for the Gazipur industrial zone, said authorities at 10 to 15 factories in Sreepur had announced two-day closures, while more than 50 other factories had declared a shutdown for Wednesday.

item.title: Awami League activists blamed as Bogra BNP office torched
item.description:
A fire was set to the Nandigram Upazila BNP office in Bogra early Wednesday, burning several party banners and festoons outside the premises.
Police and party leaders said two to three unidentified youths set fire to the office near Nandigram Filling Station around midnight. The blaze damaged banners and festoons but did not spread inside the office.
Police visited the scene with local BNP leaders around 10am on Wednesday after being informed of the incident.
Upazila BNP President Alauddin Sarker blamed Awami League activists for the attack, alleging that they had launched an arson campaign across the country. He condemned the incident and called for the arrest of those involved.
Nandigram Police Station Officer-in-Charge Tarikul Islam said efforts were under way to identify and arrest the perpetrators. Legal proceedings over the incident were also in process, he added.

item.title: Education minister: Universities should be centers of excellence, not just certificate distributors
item.description:
Universities should be centres of excellence rather than institutions merely for distributing certificates, and the education system must be skill-based and employment-oriented, Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon has said.
He made the remarks while delivering the presidential address at the 23rd meeting of the Council of the Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST) in Dhaka on Wednesday.
The education minister said the government was committed to elevating engineering education to international standards through an education system compatible with the demands of the times. The government is working to build a future generation inspired by honesty, dedication, moral values and patriotism.
He said work was underway to turn Bangladesh into an international higher education hub. The country's universities would be centres of excellence, and foreign students would also come to study there.
The minister noted that acquiring knowledge and conducting research in fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), information and communication technology (ICT), big data and robotics were essential to advancing towards the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
He expressed hope that MIST would play a leading role in taking the country forward on the path of the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
Army Chief General Waker-Uz-Zaman, Navy Chief Admiral Khondkar Misbah ul Azim, Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan, MIST Commandant Major General Md Hakimuzzaman and other relevant senior officials were present at the meeting.
After the meeting, the education minister inaugurated the MIST Sports Complex.

item.title: Attorney general: Ziaul Ahsan’s role emerges in Narayanganj seven-murder case
item.description:
Former RAB officer Ziaul Ahsan’s alleged involvement in the 2014 Narayanganj seven-murder case has emerged in the confessional statements of convicted former RAB-11 commander Tarik Sayeed Mohammad, Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal has said.
Speaking to reporters on Wednesday after the first day of the Appellate Division’s hearing on appeals in the case, the attorney general said Tarik’s statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure described Ziaul’s instructions and role in RAB operations.
According to Kazal, Tarik said no operation could be conducted without Ziaul’s approval, who was then an additional director general (operations) at RAB headquarters.
The attorney general said case records and confessional statements described how five people were abducted first. Lawyer Chandan Sarker and his driver were later abducted after witnessing the incident.
All seven were killed after being rendered unconscious, and their bodies were dumped in a river with bricks and cement bags tied to them to prevent them from floating to the surface.
Kazal said the confessions detailed the planning, abduction and killings, and were consistent with other evidence in the case. However, Ziaul was not made an accused in the trial.
He said the state had argued before the Appellate Division in favour of upholding the High Court verdict, which sentenced 15 people to death, 11 to life imprisonment and nine others to different prison terms.
Additional Attorney General Barrister Anik R Haque said the prosecution had placed before the court extracts from the confessional statements of Tarik and four other accused, as there were no eyewitnesses to the killings.
The hearing is scheduled to continue on Thursday.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,363 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,363.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified both of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,258, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The two new suspected fatalities were reported across two divisions; Mymensingh and Khulna with one death each.
A total of 1,338 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 260,528.
During the same period, 74 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 26,374.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 233,259 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 224,287 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Bangladesh’s voter count rises to 12.92cr
item.description:
Bangladesh now has 12,92,29,749 registered voters, following an update to the electoral roll ahead of the upcoming local government elections, the Election Commission (EC) has announced.
EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed disclosed the figures at the Election Commission building in Agargaon, Dhaka, on Wednesday.
The updated list includes 452,106 new voters who turned 18 by October 31.
Of the total voters, 6,58,06,574 are men, 6,34,21,878 are women and 1,297 are from the third gender, Akhtar said.
The updated electoral roll will be used in the upcoming Union Parishad and other local government elections.

item.title: Govt plans Tk1,25,378cr Dhaka-Chittagong expressway
item.description:
The government has initiated plans to turn the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway into an access-controlled expressway.
The selected design includes 64km of elevated sections and 169km at ground level, stretching from Jatrabari in Dhaka to Sagarika intersection in Chittagong. Including 20 years of operational costs, the total expenditure is projected at Tk1,25,378 crore.
The Roads and Highways Department (RHD) is preparing to implement the project under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, potentially with foreign financing through a government-to-government arrangement. Work is targeted to begin in January 2027 and finish by December 2032, subject to approval.
The highway carries around 92% of the country's international trade and 81% of its export trade. Officials say the expressway aims to ease congestion, reduce transport costs and improve connectivity with industrial zones, export processing zones and the Chittagong Port.
The plan includes a 10-lane elevated section from Dhaka to Madanpur in Narayanganj, followed by a six-lane main highway with separate lanes for local traffic. It also proposes seven system interchanges, 29 service interchanges, 91 underpasses and dedicated truck parking at 15 locations.
BUET Civil Engineering Professor Dr Md Shamsul Haque said simply widening the highway would not resolve congestion, stressing the need for an access-controlled route with reliable speed and maintenance.
However, the project's financing structure and the proportion of elevated and ground-level sections remain under review. State Minister for Road Transport and Bridges Habibur Rashid said a final decision would follow an assessment of several proposals.
RHD Additional Chief Engineer Shishir Kanti Raut said a preliminary development project proposal had been submitted to the ministry, and construction would begin after approval.

item.title: Prime Bank, Lloyds and Enigio take UK-Bangladesh digital trade to everyday scale
item.description:
Prime Bank PLC, Lloyds and Enigio have completed multiple cross-border documentary collections between Bangladesh and the UK, entirely in digital form.
Preparing the documents for the full set of collections and transferring them digitally to Lloyds took Prime Bank less than an hour, keeping turnaround time to a minimum and showing that digital trade is ready for day-to-day operations.
The shipments were made by Viyellatex Limited, one of Bangladesh's leading apparel manufacturers, to a leading UK garment wholesaler.
Prime Bank acted as remitting bank in Dhaka and Lloyds as collecting bank in the UK.
Documents for every shipment were issued and transferred on trace:original, and the buyer accepted the collections by signing digital promissory notes, also prepared on Enigio’s trace:original solution.
Lloyds also used the trace:original solution to digitally issue and transfer the release note under the air waybill which was transferred to the importer alongside the underlying collection documents.
The whole process took 48 hours from creation of the digital documents in Bangladesh to release of the documents to the buyer. No paper original or courier was involved at any stage.
Until now, cross-border digital trade on the corridor has moved one transaction at a time. Handling several collections together, with Prime Bank's work done in under an hour, turns a successful pilot into an operational channel that banks, buyers and exporters can rely on every day.
The transactions rest on Bangladesh Bank's digital trade framework, which permits electronic presentation of trade documents under approved arrangements, and on the UK Electronic Trade Documents Act 2023, which gives digital trade documents the same legal standing as paper.
“A single digital transaction proves the technology works. Doing multiple transactions together, prepared in under an hour and completed end to end in 48 hours, proves cross-border digital trade is ready for everyday business. Together with Lloyds and Enigio, we have turned digital trade between Bangladesh and the UK from an experiment into a channel our exporters can use every day,” said Faisal Rahman, managing director and CEO at Prime Bank.
“Our first digital trade transaction between Bangladesh and the UK earlier this month demonstrated what was possible; completing multiple collections digitally takes us a step further, demonstrating how digital trade can move from a single transaction to a repeatable way of doing business. By removing paper and friction from traditionally complex processes, we can make trade simpler, faster and more efficient for clients, helping digital trade become the norm rather than the exception,” said Surath Sengupta, managing director, transaction banking products at Lloyds.
“This is what digital trade at scale looks like. We still hear a lot about slow adoption, pilots and proofs of concept, but that narrative is increasingly out of step with what is actually happening. Banks and corporates are already using digital trade documents in live commercial flows, at meaningful volumes – because with trace:original, it’s easy to start, and easy to scale. The shift from experimentation to business as usual is already underway,” said Alex Waites, CCO at Enigio.
The transactions build on Prime Bank's earlier work in digital trade.
In July 2026 the bank completed Bangladesh's first eUCP and eURC governed transactions under the Bangladesh Bank pilot, and it was the first bank to place Bangladesh on the ICC global eUCP map.
Lloyds and Enigio also completed the first Documentary Collection transaction involving an electronic bill of lading in Bangladesh earlier this month with another bank in Bangladesh, demonstrating that digital trade is gaining momentum.
With these collections, Prime Bank becomes the first bank in Bangladesh to complete cross-border digital trade on both the import and the export leg.
This also shows that Prime Bank is ready to collaborate with any digital trade framework and any partner bank across the globe.

item.title: Square Pharma brings SHC100 a digital product ordering platform for local chemist shops
item.description:
Square Pharmaceuticals PLC, the country's leading pharmaceutical company, has introduced SHC100, a product ordering application designed to make medicine ordering easier, faster and more convenient for chemist shops across Bangladesh.
Muhammad Zahangir Alam, chief financial officer of Square Pharmaceuticals, shared his aspiration with a national daily, to digitalize ordering process in real time, and connect the missing “pocket” outlets, mainly in remote locations.
Through SHC100, drug stores can conveniently place orders for Square Pharmaceuticals’ products directly from their mobile devices or computers.
The initiative is enabling wider distribution network and ensuring more efficient ordering experience for its trade partners.
The introduction of SHC100 reflects Square Pharmaceuticals' continued commitment to embrace digital innovation to enhance customer convenience and operational efficiency.
As part of its future roadmap, the company is also exploring the expansion of the platform's capabilities to include home delivery services for customers.
A pilot has already been rolled out for its employees.
Apart from introducing new molecules in advanced facilities, Square Pharmaceuticals re-affirms its commitment to make healthcare more accessible through innovation and to build strong & sustainable partnerships with trade partners.

item.title: UCB retains ISO certification for business continuity management
item.description:
United Commercial Bank PLC (UCB) renewed its ISO 22301:2019 certification for its Business Continuity Management System (BCMS), retaining international recognition of its ability to maintain operational resilience and deliver uninterrupted banking services during emergencies and unexpected disruptions.
A certificate handover ceremony was recently held at UCB’s head office to mark the achievement.
Representatives of EIC, on behalf of the certifying body, British Standards Institution (BSI), handed over the renewed certificate to Nabil Mustafizur Rahman, additional managing director and chief risk officer (CRO) of UCB.
Senior management officials, divisional heads and other relevant officials of the bank attended the ceremony.
Nabil Mustafizur Rahman, AMD and CRO of UCB, said: “Financial institutions today must remain prepared to address various risks and unexpected disruptions. The renewal of our ISO 22301:2019 certification reflects UCB’s continued efforts to maintain operational continuity and deliver uninterrupted banking services to customers, even under challenging circumstances. We remain committed to our customers, stakeholders and business partners.”
ISO 22301:2019 is an internationally recognized standard for business continuity management.
It provides organizations with a structured framework to prepare for emergencies and major disruptions, maintain critical operations and restore normal activities as quickly as possible.
The standard also helps organizations identify potential risks, strengthen preparedness and enhance their ability to respond effectively to unexpected situations.
To ensure business continuity, UCB continues to strengthen its risk management practices, technology infrastructure and alternative operational arrangements.
The bank has established disaster recovery facilities, secure technology infrastructure and structured emergency response plans.
It also regularly conducts business continuity exercises, disaster recovery tests and employee awareness training to ensure preparedness across the organization.
The successful recertification reaffirms UCB’s commitment to delivering secure, reliable and customer-focused banking services while maintaining internationally recognized standards in business continuity management.

item.title: bKash launches ‘Experience Zone’ at Brac University
item.description:
bKash has launched an ‘Experience Zone’ at Brac University, giving students, faculty members and staffs easy access to a wide range of bKash services on campus.
The two organizations also signed a memorandum of understanding to advance the university’s cashless campus initiative, enabling all kinds of transactions from semester fees to making payment at canteen through bKash.
Prof Syed Ferhat Anwar, vice-chancellor of Brac University and Kamal Quadir, chief executive officer of bKash recently inaugurated the Experience Zone at the university’s Badda campus in the capital.
Ariful Islam, treasurer of Brac University, David Austin Dowland, registrar, Md Mashrur Rahim Sadat, director of finance and accounts, Azharul Islam Bhuiyan, joint director, finance and accounts of Brac University; Ali Ahmmed, chief commercial officer of bKash, Mir Nawbut Ali, chief marketing officer of bKash, and senior officials from both organizations attended the event.
The experience zone has established to provide uninterrupted services to over 20,000 students, faculty members, officers and employees of the university.
Users can get instant services such as cash in, cash out, account registration, savings, assisted microfinance and remittance services, PIN reset and unblock, information updates, account activation and statements, along with other account-related services.
As part of the cashless campus initiative, students can use bKash to pay semester fee, library fee, laboratory fee, activity and transport fees, as well as make payments at the cafeteria, canteens and stationery shops.
The initiative reduces the need to carry cash while making everyday transactions across the campus faster and seamless. It will also help students to get oriented with cashless ecosystem.
At the same time, digital payments are expected to make the university’s administrative processes and financial management simpler and more transparent.
Brac University VC Prof Syed Ferhat Anwar said: “This joint initiative with bKash will play an effective role in bringing all transactions, from semester fees to everyday payments across the campus, under a digital system. The two organizations will also work together to engage students more actively and help them become accustomed to digital transactions.”
CEO of bKash Kamal Quadir said: “Effective solutions emerge when users’ actual needs and pain points are properly addressed. In the early days, people adopted mobile financial services primarily to meet essential financial solutions. Gradually, convenience also became a key driver of adoption. This initiative with Brac University can become a good example for bKash to demonstrate the same to other universities.”
Education fees for schools, colleges, universities, online courses and training institutes can be paid through bKash from anywhere.
Students and guardians no longer need to visit institutions or wait in queues to make such payments.
Once a payment is completed, they receive an instant notification and a digital receipt.

item.title: New pay structure for RMG workers: Who gets how much
item.description:
The Minimum Wage Board has finalized a new wage structure for ready-made garment (RMG) workers, which is set to take effect on December 1.
Under the new structure, wages for the lowest grade have been raised by Tk4,500, while the highest increase of Tk6,465 has been approved for Grade 1 (Senior Operator).
The decisions were made at the fourth meeting of the board, which continued until late Tuesday night at the Minimum Wage Board office in Dhaka’s Segunbagicha.
Following nearly 10 hours of discussions -- starting at 3:15pm and ending around 1:30am -- wages for three grades were fixed unanimously, while the lowest grade was decided through a vote. Multiple board members later confirmed the new pay structure.
According to the revised structure, the gross monthly wage for Grade 1 (Senior Operator) has been set at Tk21,500, up from Tk15,035, marking an increase of Tk6,465.
For Grade 2 (Operator), wages have been increased by Tk5,727 to Tk20,000, compared to the previous Tk14,273.
Workers in Grade 3 (Junior Operator) will receive Tk19,200, up from Tk13,550 -- an increase of Tk5,650. Meanwhile, the minimum wage for the lowest grade has been fixed at Tk17,000, rising by Tk4,500 from the previous Tk12,500.
During the meeting, factory owners initially revised their proposal to Tk17,000 while labor representatives proposed Tk18,000.
As both sides remained firm on their stances, owners eventually lowered their offer to Tk16,000, prompting Board Chairman Syed Azad Subhani to call for a vote.
Out of six board members who cast votes, the two labor representatives voted for Tk18,000, while the remaining four members voted in favor of Tk17,000, finalizing the lowest minimum wage at Tk17,000.
Briefing reporters at 4:00am after the meeting, Chairman Syed Azad Subhani said the board will hold another meeting to finalize the breakdown of basic salary and house rent within the gross wages.
